deployNotes: This is a static frontend application; the build step (vite build) produces dist/ which nginx serves as static files.
The production Dockerfile is multi-stage: node:20-alpine builds the assets, nginx:alpine serves them. For Nexlayer, the runtime pod only needs the nginx stage.
No inter-pod communication is needed as there is no backend or database.
No database pod is required — all data is client-side (mock or embedded).

productionPlan.summary: A single nginx pod serves the pre-built static Vite/React dashboard. There is no backend, database, or persistent data — the entire app is client-side with mock analytics. The one thing that matters most is ensuring the build step produces dist/ and nginx serves it correctly.

decisions.decision: One web pod running nginx to serve the static Vite build output from /usr/share/nginx/html
decisions.why: The Dockerfile's production stage is nginx:alpine serving static files, and the nginx.conf has SPA fallback (try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html) — no other services are needed

decisions.decision: Use the existing multi-stage Dockerfile: node:20-alpine runs vite build to produce dist/, then nginx:alpine serves it
decisions.why: The Dockerfile already correctly builds the Vite app and copies dist/ into the nginx image at /usr/share/nginx/html

decisions.decision: Single pod listens on port 80 and receives all external traffic at path /
decisions.why: nginx.conf listens on port 80 and the nginx.conf SPA rewrite rule handles all routes

decisions.decision: No volumes — the app serves only static build artifacts with no uploads, no database, no state to persist
decisions.why: There are no external_deps, no database, and all analytics data is client-side mock or embedded in the bundle

fix_before_production.title: Commit package-lock.json or change npm ci to npm install in the Dockerfile
fix_before_production.why: No package-lock.json appears in the repository tree, but the Dockerfile runs `npm ci` which fails without a lockfile — the build will crash

verify_after_deploy: GET / on the app URL returns HTTP 200 and an HTML page containing the cyberpunk analytics dashboard markup
GET /assets/index-*.js (or similar hashed JS bundle) returns HTTP 200 with Content-Type containing 'javascript'
A request to an unknown route like /nonexistent-page returns the same index.html (SPA fallback works)
productionPlan.nexlayer_yaml:
application:
  name: cyberpunk-analytics
  pods:
    - name: web
      image: "registry.nexlayer.io/YOUR_USER_ID/cyberpunk-analytics-web:planned"
      path: /
      servicePorts:
        - 80
      vars: {}
